what_happened: On 2026-11-02 the the person running Athena raised the "keep the writer's work on timeout" fix to urgent priority. The balance-shards job (20261031-230917-g47x) had just become the fourth job that week to lose all its work when the producer (writer) hit its 50-minute limit. Each loss cost a full writer run. This was a hand change to the queue, outside any job. No acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed for the event.
cause: A producer timeout throws away all partial work, and the fix that would keep it was queued at ordinary priority with nothing tying it to the repeated losses. Athena does not count timeout losses per class, so it never raises the fix's priority itself. The earlier case showed the same pattern: six losses, a deadline raised by hand, and the keep-work fix itself timing out. Athena has no signal that connects repeated deadline losses to the priority of the fix. The the person running Athena has to notice the pattern and re-rank by hand. Unbounded priority use (20261031-082316-0bss) also makes a manual raise the only way to signal urgency.
prevention: Make a producer deadline hit non-destructive. On timeout, commit the working tree to a work-in-progress branch, record it in the job's records, and mark the job held or resumable, not failed. A retry then resumes from that work. As a second part, count deadline losses per week and have Athena automatically raise the keep-work fix (and any job that splits oversized work) once a set threshold, such as three, is crossed.
proposed_request: When the producer hits its time deadline, keep its work instead of discarding it. Outcome: a job that times out is left held with its partial changes saved on a branch and listed in the job's records, and `athena retry` resumes from that saved work rather than starting over. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake producer that runs past the deadline shows the changes are saved and the job state is held, not failed; (2) a retry of that job starts from the saved changes; (3) the job's records state that the stop was a timeout, with the elapsed time and the files saved; (4) a producer that finishes in time behaves as before. Also add a count of deadline losses per week, and have Athena show a warning when it reaches three. Use only existing config fields. Do not change the deadline value.
